title: qBTC: A Post-Quantum Bitcoin Protocol — Reference Implementation
description: qBTC is a complete reimplementation of the Bitcoin protocol engineered for the post-quantum era. It replaces all Shor-vulnerable cryptographic primitives (ECDSA/secp256k1) with NIST-standardized post-quantum algorithms — ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) for digital signatures, SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) as a hash-based fallback, and ML-KEM-1024 (FIPS 203) for key encapsulation — while replacing SHA-256 with SHA3-256 for Grover-resistant hashing. The protocol introduces a three-phase hybrid consensus mechanism transitioning from Quantum Proof-of-Work to hybrid QPoW+PoS to pure Proof-of-Stake, with a 64-bit mining nonce that neutralizes Grover's quadratic speedup. This repository contains the full reference implementation including: post-quantum cryptographic primitives, blockchain data structures, hybrid consensus engine, SHA3-256d mining engine, async TCP P2P networking, quantum-resistant HD wallet with Bech32m addresses, JSON-RPC 2.0 API, CLI, Docker deployment, and a comprehensive test suite.

subjects.term: Computer Science — Distributed, Parallel, and Cluster Computing

notes: This software is a research prototype implementing a post-quantum secure blockchain protocol. It uses the Open Quantum Safe liboqs library for NIST-standardized post-quantum cryptographic operations. The protocol is designed as a proof-of-concept and has not undergone formal security auditing. The 64-bit nonce space and SHA3-256 hashing provide equivalent mining difficulty to classical Bitcoin under Grover's algorithm analysis.
